highlights.title: 监督搜索过程，而不是监督最终答案
highlights.title_en: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
highlights.summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

highlights.section: LLM 多智能体与社会模拟
highlights.glance: 把奖励从「答对没有」挪到「这一步搜得好不好」，搜索智能体的域外泛化随之显著增强

essay.v: 一个检索问答智能体答对了题目，却被发现压根没读过它引用的任何一篇文档——它靠参数记忆蒙对了答案。这类「蒙对」在结果监督下拿到满分奖励，于是被反复强化；一旦换到训练时没见过的领域，记忆失效，分数就塌了。更麻烦的是，搜索的每一步到底该不该做、该搜什么，模型从没被教过。这篇顶刊文章的出发点正是这个矛盾：奖励给错了地方，学出来的就只能是会偷懒的检索器。
把「这一步好不好」变成可训练的偏好

作者搭的框架叫 RAG-Gym。它把搜索智能体看成一套决策过程：每个时刻可以发起一次检索，也可以直接给答案。接下来要解决的问题是过程奖励从哪来。最常见的做法是让智能体滚出多条完整轨迹，用最终成败反推每一步的价值，也就是基于采样的过程奖励模型。作者试了，结果很糟：在 2Wiki 多跳问答上，这种奖励训出来的评论家引导推理只拿到 55.6 的 F1 基线之下，而靠大模型标注信号训出的评论家能到 57.9。原因就是开头那个陷阱——答案猜对了，轨迹本身却是无关的，采样法会把噪声当成正样本。

换成强模型当裁判之后情况就变了。做法是：先让未微调的智能体采样多条轨迹，只保留最终答案正确的那批；再在每个状态上采样若干候选动作，请裁判按三条标准给这些动作排序——历史信息已经足够回答问题时应偏好直接作答、查询要精确可操作、以及优先能带来新信息的动作。排序结果构成偏好元组，既能做偏好优化，也能训练独立的评论家。医学问答基准上，这套标注与人类判断的一致性做到 85.8%，说明标准是可复现的，不是裁判的随意发挥。
六个模块里，缺的那一个最要紧
作者把搜索智能体的能力拆成六块：答案生成、问题推理、检索增强、查询生成、文档摘要，以及推理反思。把常见基线挨个对照会发现，直接作答、思维链、朴素检索增强、以及两种代表性的检索智能体都少了最后一块。所谓推理反思，是先起草一条答案推理链，找出其中第一个没有被当前历史支持的论断，再把这个论断改写成一次定向检索查询——搜索的动机来自逻辑上的必要，而不是「再多搜一句可能有用」。
这个设计带来的增益不只出现在最终分数上。补齐反思模块后，同一套框架在零样本、监督微调、偏好优化、策略梯度四种训练机制下，四个基准上持续领先五个基线，说明这是一条真实的归纳偏置，而不是某个训练技巧的偶然产物。数据效率也相当高：通用域基准只需要 250 条过程奖励样本就能显著超过零样本基线；医学域呈 U 型曲线，大约要到 1000 条才到峰值。
域外泛化，以及小模型管大模型
最值得记的一条结果在域外。与两个结果监督路线的检索智能体相比，新方法在训练分布内持平或略好，但在完全没见过的基准上泛化明显更强：检索召回率更高，而且是用相当甚至更少的搜索步数换来的。换句话说，它学到的东西不是「这道题该怎么答」，而是「什么时候该搜、该搜什么」。作者还报告偏好优化相对监督微调平均带来几个百分点的提升，这个量级在检索问答上并不小。
推理时扩展也有一组反直觉的数字。每个决策点采样多个候选动作、由评论家挑最好的执行，准确率随候选数上升，但会在 15 到 20 之间饱和：医学问答上 15 个候选时最好，加到 20 个反而回落。作者的解释是候选变多会诱发奖励攻击——模型学会生成评分很高但语义上有缺陷的动作。所以他们建议把候选数定在 10 到 15，而不是一味加大。
另一条可以立刻落地的结果是跨模型迁移：只用开源小模型的轨迹训练出来的评论家，不需要重新训练，就能给一个商业大模型当引导，把医学问答准确率从 76.8 提到 78.1。这意味着「什么样的搜索是好的」是一件可以独立训练、独立部署的能力，用便宜的开源评论家去管昂贵的大模型是一条现实的工程路径。
怎么读这篇

这是 Nature Communications 的正式发表版，2026 年 10 月 28 日上线，十二位作者，开源预印本与代码库都可查，预印本在 2025 年 2 月首发、2026 年 5 月最后一次修订，两者标题与结论一致。本次核实只取到页面公开的完整摘要与部分正文数字，逐基准的表格仍以正文与附录为准，引用具体数值前建议回到原文核对。另外，医学基准上的人类一致性标注由具备医学背景的共同作者完成，属于团队内部一致性，不等同于外部盲评。
对做检索智能体或任何多步工具调用系统的团队，这篇给的最实用的一条是奖励设计的反面教材：凡是最终指标可以被「绕过去」得手的任务，基于采样的过程奖励都会失灵，改用强模型对候选动作做排序反而稳。其次是把「搜索决策」当成一门可独立训练的能力，用小模型训、给大模型用，比端到端重训整个智能体便宜得多。

highlights.title: 只知道估值的上下限时，最优拍卖长什么样
highlights.title_en: Robust Auction Design with Support Information
highlights.summary: A seller wants to sell an item to n buyers. Buyer valuations are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) according to a distribution unknown to the seller; the seller only knows that the support is included in [a, b]. To be robust, the seller chooses a dominant strategy incentive compatible mechanism that optimizes the worst-case performance relative to the ideal expected revenue the seller could have collected with knowledge of buyers’ valuations. Our analysis unifies the regret and the ratio objectives. For these objectives, we derive an optimal mechanism and the corresponding performance in quasi-closed form, as a function of the support information [a, b] and the number of buyers n. Our analysis reveals three regimes of support information and a new class of robust mechanisms. (i) When a/b is below a threshold, the optimal mechanism is a second-price auction (SPA) with random reserve, a focal class in earlier literature. (ii) When a/b is above another threshold, SPAs are strictly suboptimal, and an optimal mechanism belongs to a class of mechanisms we introduce, which we call pooling auctions (POOL); whenever the highest value is above a threshold, the mechanism still allocates to the highest bidder, but otherwise the mechanism allocates to a uniformly random buyer, that is, pools low types. (iii) When a/b is between two thresholds, a randomization between SPA and POOL is optimal. We also characterize optimal mechanisms within nested central subclasses of mechanisms: standard mechanisms that only allocate to the highest bidder, SPA with random reserve, and SPA with no reserve. We show strict separations in terms of performance across classes, implying that deviating from standard mechanisms is necessary for robustness. Lastly, we show that the same results hold under other distribution classes that capture “positive dependence,” namely i.i.d., mixture of i.i.d., and exchangeable and affiliated distributions, as well as i.i.d. regular distributions. This paper was accepted by David Simchi-Levi, revenue management and market analytics. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.02703 .

highlights.glance: 最优鲁棒机制随支撑上下限比值分成三段，高端区间里二价拍卖严格次优，取而代之的是「池化拍卖」

essay.v: 最优拍卖的经典结论有一个前提：卖家知道买家的估值分布。现实里这个前提几乎从不成立——你能说出的往往只有一句「大概在十万到三十万之间」。可一旦承认分布未知，传统理论就失了靶心：既没有分布可代入，也没法定义什么是最优。这篇 Management Science 的文章把问题重新钉住，然后给出了一套拟闭式的最优解。
与「理想收益」比，而不是与「最差情形」比
设定很干净：一个卖家、一件物品、n 个买家，估值独立同分布但分布对卖家未知，唯一的公共信息是支撑落在区间 [a, b] 之内。卖家要选一个占优策略激励相容的机制，目标是最坏情况下相对于「理想收益」的表现——也就是假如卖家事后知道所有估值本可以收上来的期望收入。这样定义的好处是它把两类常用目标统一了：收益之差与收益之比。以这两个目标为尺，作者把最优机制与对应表现写成支撑区间与买家人数的拟闭式函数。
这里有个容易被忽略的建模选择值得强调：基准不是「什么都不做」，而是「全知者能拿到多少」。所以机制被追问的是「你因为无知损失了多少」，而不是「最坏能有多惨」。用这个尺子量出来的最优机制，和用绝对最坏收益量出来的并不一样，前者更贴近平台的真实决策情境。
三段结构：到了某个点，二价拍卖就不够用了
结论按 a 与 b 的比值分成三段。比值低到某个门槛以下时，最优机制是带随机保留价的二价拍卖，这正是早期鲁棒拍卖文献聚焦的那类机制。比值高到另一个门槛以上时，二价拍卖严格次优，最优者属于作者新引入的一类机制，他们称之为池化拍卖：当最高估值超过某个门槛时仍分配给最高出价者，否则就把物品均匀随机地分给某个买家，也就是把所有低类型买家「池化」处理。两个门槛之间，最优的是二价拍卖与池化拍卖的随机化。
池化拍卖的直觉值得琢磨。当你对买家估值几乎一无所知时，去分辨「谁稍微高一点」的价值很低，反而会因为机制复杂而损失确定性收入；不如对低估值区间干脆放弃甄别，只在高估值出现时才认真分配。这是把「信息不足」直接写进机制结构，而不是靠调参去补偿。
作者还做了几层嵌套子类的刻画：只分配给最高出价者的标准机制、带随机保留价的二价拍卖、无保留价的二价拍卖。结果是这些类别之间的表现存在严格分离，意味着想获得鲁棒性，就必须离开标准机制的舒适区——不是调参数能解决的差距。最后，同一套结论被证明在若干刻画「正相依」的分布类上都成立，包括独立同分布、独立同分布的混合、可交换且仿射附属的分布，以及独立同分布的正则分布。
怎么读这篇

这是 Management Science 的正式发表版，由收益管理与市场分析方向的编辑处理，三位作者中有两位长期在这个领域做动态定价与在线机制设计，公开渠道能核到卷期与在线附录。需要注意的是：文中给出的是拟闭式解与结构刻画，具体数值要查在线附录，别只看主文的三段描述就下结论。另外，同一批作者还有一篇聚焦确定性机制的姊妹论文，今天也被雷达抓到，两篇合起来才是完整的故事。本文不含实证部分，全部结论建立在分布族假设之上，把它用在真实拍卖平台前需要先验证你的买家估值是否落在「正相依」这一侧。
给做拍卖与定价的人留一条可操作的判据：先量一下你能给出的估值上下限比值落在哪一段。低端区间按老办法用带随机保留价的二价拍卖即可；一旦进入高端区间，坚持二价拍卖就是明确的效率损失，此时「对低估值干脆不做甄别」反而是最优的。更广义地说，当先验信息弱到只剩区间时，最优机制往往长得很反直觉，此时该改的是机制族，不是超参数。

highlights.title: 经典紧握拍卖天然抗女巫，以及由此造出的抗夹子攻击做市机制
highlights.title_en: Sybil-Proofness of Generalized Adaptive Clinching and Implications for Blockchain Mechanism Design
highlights.summary: The adaptive clinching auction of Dobzinski, Lavi, and Nisan (FOCS'08) is a cornerstone of mechanism design with budget-constrained bidders, and it has since inspired a broad range of extensions to substantially richer market settings. Adaptive clinching enjoys compelling guarantees: it is Pareto optimal, and truthful bidding is a dominant strategy whenever budgets cannot be overreported. In many real-world environments, however, identities are cheap to create, making resilience to Sybil attacks an additional requirement. Whether the guarantees of adaptive clinching survive when a bidder can split its budget across fake identities has remained open. We introduce a generalized framework for adaptive clinching and prove that it satisfies Sybil-robust incentive compatibility: a bidder cannot benefit from splitting into any finite number of identities with arbitrary value reports, provided their aggregate reported budget does not exceed the bidder's enforceable true budget. Sybil resilience thus joins the list of ideal properties of adaptive clinching. Our work is motivated by practical problems in decentralized finance, where automated market makers (AMMs) are among the most widely used applications. We design a new AMM mechanism that extends classical adaptive clinching in two ways: it supports a two-sided market and protects against two-sided strategies, and it allows the supply function to depend on the auction state. Its one-sided special case is captured by our generalized adaptive clinching framework, and our proof techniques show that the full two-sided mechanism simultaneously satisfies Sybil-robust incentive compatibility and a relaxed notion of Pareto optimality. We argue that these guarantees are essentially the best possible via impossibility results. More broadly, our work reveals new connections between classical algorithmic game theory and modern decentralized blockchains.
highlights.summary_short: The adaptive clinching auction of Dobzinski, Lavi, and Nisan (FOCS'08) is a cornerstone of mechanism design with budget-constrained bidders, and it has since inspired a broad range of extensions to substantially richer market settings.
highlights.glance: 证明了 2008 年的经典自适应紧握拍卖不可被分身套利，并据此设计出一个同时抗女巫、抗重排序的双边做市机制

essay.v: 链上世界的身份成本接近于零，注册十个钱包比注册一个账号还便宜。这让经典机制设计里「一人一身份」的默认假设直接失效：一个买家可以把预算拆到一百个身份上，去试探、去套利。自适应紧握拍卖是预算受限买家下最著名的机制之一，它帕累托最优、且只要预算不能虚报就说实话即占优。但它扛不扛分身术？这个问题一直悬着，直到这篇给出了肯定答案。
先把一个经典结果提升成一族框架
作者的思路不是直接证明某一个机制的抗性，而是先把自适应紧握拍卖抽象成一套基于目标的框架。经典版本假设存在一个固定外生的可分配供给量；而在自动化做市商的设定里根本没有固定供给——定价曲线决定了此刻能交易多少，供给是机制状态的函数。于是他们把「目标」换成由成本曲线与当前状态共同决定的量，供给随状态演化这一件事就被吸收进了框架。经典的可分割固定供给拍卖、以及外生在线供给的扩展，都成为这套框架的特例。

这样抽象的好处是抗女巫性只需在框架层面证明一次，框架内所有机制就都继承了这个性质。具体保证是这样一句话：以单一身份诚实参与，弱占优于任何「拆成任意有限多个身份、任意虚报估值」的偏离策略，前提是所有同方向的申报预算加起来不超过该买家真实的、可被强制执行的预算。对反方向的女巫预算则没有上限要求。这个前提不是白拿的——它要求申报预算由托管资金支撑，且托管不能在同一批次里用另一个身份的收益去补。文中还给出一个推论：抗女巫的激励相容隐含了「没有免费午餐」，任何身份子集都不可能在一个资产上净赚而不在另一个资产上亏损，这直接排除了纯套利型的区块构造者。
造一个抗夹子攻击的双边做市机制
论文的现实动机是去中心化金融里的矿工可提取价值：区块构造者可以凭对交易包含与排序的单边控制，用前跑加后跑的夹子攻击无风险获利，已有测量研究指出以太坊上最大的两家构造者产出了超过八成的区块。作者设计的做市机制在两个方向上扩展了经典紧握拍卖：一是支持双边市场，买单与卖单可以互相撮合，残余失衡与流动性池结算；二是允许供给函数依赖拍卖状态。
其中「与顺序无关」这一条是专门对着区块构造者去的：机制结果与批次内交易排序无关，重排序自然就无从获利。结算上要求储备精确回到储备曲线，不补贴也不销毁；效率上做到对合格出价的弱帕累托最优，只排除合格交易者之间的再交易。实现层面作者提醒了一个工程细节——防预算超额申报的托管必须防闪电贷攻击，可行的办法是把托管与结算分到不同区块执行。
结果好到什么程度？不可能性定理给出了边界

作者并没有止步于「我们做到了」，而是给出了两条说明这就是极限的不可能性结果。其一：如果允许任意虚报估值与预算，那么任何确定性做市机制都不可能同时满足抗女巫激励相容与弱帕累托最优。这个否定结论的强度尤其值得注意——它的构造只需要替换单一一个卖出报告的偏离，既不需要多个女巫身份，也不需要反方向的订单，甚至即便机制能拿到每笔出价上不可伪造的辅助信息（比如可信时间戳）也依然成立。其二：如果坚持完全的帕累托最优，那么即便禁止同方向预算超额申报，不可能性仍然存在。
两条合起来意味着：要么放松效率，要么放松对虚报的容忍度，二者不可兼得。文中还点明了与已有工作的关系——先前有一类抗女巫机制达不到弱帕累托最优，还依赖可信到达时间戳，而时间戳本身易被操纵；另有一条三难定理说明激励相容、弱局部效率与统一定价三者不可兼得，澄清了「批次统一定价就等于抗夹子」这个流行误解；还有工作靠允许销毁来换取完全帕累托最优，本文则坚持严格精确结算。
怎么读这篇

这是 2026 年 10 月 27 日的预印本，跨计算机科学与博弈论、理论经济学两个分类，六位作者里有做密码学与区块链系统的，也有做社会选择与机制设计理论的。要注意它的性质：纯理论工作，没有实现、没有实验、没有链上数据验证；结论依赖两个前提——共识层提供抗审查保证，以及预算托管可以真正强制执行。这两个前提在真实公链上都不是免费的。另外文中「两台构造者产出超八成区块」这类测量数字来自引用的文献，反映的是特定时段的观测，会随时间变化。
最值得迁移的一条思路是前提的替换：与其假设「身份不可伪造」这种在链上根本不成立的东西，不如假设「预算托管可执行」——后者是可以用工程手段真正落实的弱前提，而它就足以支撑抗女巫性。另一条是这篇展示的双向通道：经典算法博弈论里二十年前的工具，正在链上机制设计里找到新问题；反过来，区块链的约束也在倒逼经典理论补上以前不必回答的定理。

highlights.title: 所有广告主同时无遗憾，在计算上做不到
highlights.title_en: Impossibility of No-Regret in Multi-Agent Bidding
highlights.summary: We consider $T$ repeated second-price auctions across $n$ pacing bidders with i.i.d. item arrivals, and show that it is computationally impossible for all bidders to achieve no-regret simultaneously while satisfying their respective budget or return-on-investment constraints. Therefore, in the prominent internet auction systems where buyers simultaneously deploy pacing algorithms or automated bidding agents, we cannot hope to achieve joint no-regret guarantees in general. We establish a deterministic relationship that high variance in online bidding systems implies high regret. By showing that one can extract a pacing equilibrium from a low-variance system, we prove PPAD-hardness of attaining joint no-regret. For several widely used bidding algorithms, we also show evidence from dynamical systems and numerical simulations that they can indeed display high-variance behavior through cycling, even on simple market instances.
highlights.summary_short: We consider $T$ repeated second-price auctions across $n$ pacing bidders with i.i.d. item arrivals, and show that it is computationally impossible for all bidders to achieve no-regret simultaneously while satisfying their respective budget or return-on-investment constraints.
highlights.glance: 在自动竞价市场里，让所有买家同时接近事后最优是 PPAD 难的，乘子的高波动本身就意味着线性遗憾

essay.v: 广告平台向广告主推销自动竞价服务时，隐含着一个承诺：用我们的算法，你长期下来的收益会接近「假如你当时什么都知晓」的最优水平。单个买家面对独立同分布的市场，这个承诺是成立的，次线性遗憾的算法一抓一把。但把 n 个都跑着调价算法的买家放进同一个市场，这个承诺还成立吗？这篇的答案是：除非能多项式时间解决 PPAD 难问题，否则至少有一个买家的遗憾会随时间线性增长，或者预算与投资回报约束被大幅违反。
设定：二价拍卖、调价乘子、预算与回报率约束
市场是 T 轮重复的二价拍卖，每轮一件物品，价值向量独立同分布地到达，但同一轮内买家之间允许相关。买家分两类：一类是在预算约束下最大化效用，另一类是在投资回报率约束下最大化总价值。所谓调价策略，指的是买家在看到本轮价值之前先选一个乘子，出价等于乘子乘以自己的估值——这正是主流自动竞价系统在用的形式。值得注意的是，作者甚至允许平台把所有买家的乘子集中协调，结论依然不变。
遗憾的基准是事后最优：在对手乘子序列固定时，该买家逐轮「赢或不赢」的最优选择。于是主定理的每个版本都在说同一件事：存在某个实例，使得至少一个买家的期望遗憾或期望约束违反量超过 T 除以买家数量的一个次多项式量级。由于这个次多项式量级可以任意接近线性，参与者变多并不能显著摊薄遗憾；而且结论对任意多项式规模的轮数都成立，直接排除了常见的次线性遗憾目标。
方差与遗憾之间是一条确定性不等式
全文最有工程价值的部分，是把调价乘子重新解释成一个原始—对偶算法里的对偶变量。在这个视角下，作者给出一个确定性的三项分解：事后最优与实际所得之差，等于线性化间隙加上互补松弛项再减去对偶间隙。由此推出的关键定理是：当对偶损失强凸时，遗憾不小于强凸常数的一半乘以对偶变量的累计方差。换句话说，乘子振荡得越厉害，遗憾就越大，而且是硬性的下界，不是经验规律。
这条不等式配上「互补松弛非负」这一事实，就得到了一个可以立刻上线的监控指标：平台不需要计算遗憾，只要盯住自家调价乘子的波动幅度，就能判断系统是不是正在走向线性遗憾。反过来，要从低遗憾推出低方差，再配合低预算违反与小互补松弛，就能从在线历史里反推出一个近似的调价均衡；而计算这种均衡恰恰是 PPAD 难的，矛盾于是成立。
这里有一个容易被混淆的地方值得点明：在标准的正规形式博弈里，哪怕纳什均衡是 PPAD 难的，多个玩家同时做到无遗憾仍然是可能的，因为无遗憾学习收敛到的是粗相关均衡一类更弱的概念。这篇说明拍卖加调价约束的设定本质上不同——预算与回报率约束把「无遗憾」这个概念挤压到了必须接近真实均衡的位置，于是计算困难就顺着这条缝隙渗了进来。
连三个买家都能让它们转圈

理论之外，作者用动力系统与数值仿真补上了证据。他们取了一个只有三个买家、价值分布近似于石头剪刀布的实例：每轮物品都被估值最高的买家拿走，价格却由估值次高的买家决定。于是出现一条闭环——某人出价抬高，另一人花费变多、下轮下调，第三人又随之变化，绕回原点。在这条循环上，无论用连续时间的比例积分控制器，还是离散时间的在线镜像下降（欧氏更新或熵更新、固定学习率或按时间根号分之一衰减），调价乘子都会持续振荡，累计遗憾随时间线性增长。规模提醒很直接：循环只需要三个买家就能触发。
怎么读这篇

这是 2026 年 10 月 27 日的预印本，作者来自哥伦比亚大学与卡内基梅隆大学，长期做在线机制设计与市场均衡计算。需要说明的是：不可能性是「存在实例」意义上的，不是说任何市场都会出现线性遗憾；仿真部分只在构造出来的小规模实例上跑，没有真实广告平台的日志验证。另外文中出现的「不存在多个买家同时低遗憾的多项式时间算法」这一表述要按原文的随机化归约来理解，指的是除非 PPAD 难问题存在多项式时间的随机算法。作者在致谢里还明确声明，用大模型工具改进了证明中的常数并简化附录计算，但强调这不构成实质性贡献——这种披露方式本身也值得留意。
给做自动竞价产品的人两条落地的东西。第一是画红线：联合无遗憾这件事不能写进对广告主的承诺，因为它是计算困难而非算法不够好。第二是换指标：既然方差与遗憾之间有确定性下界，就把调价乘子的波动幅度做成线上告警，比事后统计遗憾便宜得多，也早得多。方法层面，「均衡难算所以学习动力学也不可能学得很好」这条归约思路，可以搬到任何带约束的在线学习市场里去试。

highlights.title: 同一个评论家读两遍：何时该撤掉中心化指导
highlights.title_en: TANDEM: Balancing Centralized and Decentralized Critics to Address the Information Gap in Complex Multi-Agent Environments
highlights.summary: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) shapes decentralized policies with a centralized critic that observes the global state, then removes the critic at execution. The policies are optimized to rely on information they will not have when they act, an information gap between training and execution. It widens under partial observability, observation noise, and openness, where the set of agents and tasks present changes during an episode. Existing methods transfer centralized guidance in one direction only, removing or distilling the critic once, so the policies never rehearse acting without the critic while they can still be corrected. We propose TANDEM, which keeps one centralized critic and reads it two ways at each training step: a centralized read from the global state, and a decentralized read restricted to the information each agent will have at execution. A parameter-free gate compares the two reads for each agent and trains the policy on the decentralized read where they agree, reinstating the centralized read only where the local view is misleading. A shared target pulls the decentralized read toward the centralized one. We formalize the setting as a task- and agent-open decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (TAO-Dec-POMDP) and evaluate TANDEM on three cooperative domains, each isolating one form of the information gap: discovery for partial observability, sampling for observation noise, and openness in wildfire suppression. We compare against six CTDE baselines and ablate the gate and the shared target; the supplementary material holds the full variant sweep, diagnostics, and learning curves. We measure return at execution, once the centralized critic is removed. TANDEM is the best method on eight of the nine setups and never significantly worse than any baseline.
highlights.summary_short: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) shapes decentralized policies with a centralized critic that observes the global state, then removes the critic at execution.
tags: 中心化训练去中心化执行
highlights.glance: 一个评论家做两次读取，用符号是否一致的免参数门决定每一步该按本地视角还是全局视角训练策略

essay.v: 中心化训练、去中心化执行这套范式有个一直被默认忽略的裂缝：训练时策略由一个能看见全局状态的评论家带着学，可一到执行，这个评论家就被摘掉了。策略等于被优化去依赖一种它在真正干活时并不拥有的信息。部分可观测、观测噪声、以及智能体与任务在回合中途进进出出的开放场景，都会把这道裂缝撑大。更尴尬的是，现有办法——一次性蒸馏、按固定时间表衰减、随机丢弃消息——都是单向的：指导给出去就收不回来，策略从来没有在「还能被纠正的时候」演练过没有评论家该怎么走。
先把场景写清楚：连任务都会变的开放环境
作者把问题形式化成一类任务与智能体双重开放的去中心化部分可观测马尔可夫决策过程。它在已有的「智能体开放」设定上加了一层任务开放：状态里额外携带当前存在的任务集合，而每个动作只有在对应任务存在时才可用，否则只能选择空操作。观测也相应扩展，把「哪些动作现在可用」如实告诉智能体，噪声只扰动观测本身而不污染可用性信息。火场里灭火剂耗尽的队员被迫退出、新的火点被点燃或蔓延熄灭，都可以落进这个形式化里。
一个评论家，两种读法
方法的核心是一个评论家读两遍。评论家建立在实体令牌上的注意力编码器之上，天然支持智能体与任务数量变化。第一遍是集中读取，喂进完整的令牌集合；第二遍是分散读取，用掩码把这个智能体观测不到的令牌遮掉，于是它只依赖执行时真正拥有的信息。两次读取各自算出优势估计。
接下来是一道免参数的门：比较两次读取给出的优势符号。符号一致，说明本地视角此刻并不误导，门就关上，策略直接在分散优势上训练——相当于把评论家临时撤回；符号不一致，说明本地视角正在把策略带偏，门就按分歧幅度重新引入集中读取来纠正。混合后的优势送进裁剪式的策略更新。作者还给两条读取配了同一个回归目标，让分散读取逐步逼近集中读取，于是评论家是被逐个智能体、逐步地撤走的，而不是按预先写死的时间表。
这套设计的成本很低：门没有新增参数，执行时的开销与纯去中心化的行动者完全一致，训练侧只是评论家多了一次前向。这一点对工程落地很关键，因为它意味着可以直接插到现有的中心化训练框架上。
九个设置里八个最好，但也把不好看的地方写出来了
实验安排在三个合作域上，每个域各自隔离一种信息鸿沟：目标发现域隔离部分可观测，采样域隔离观测噪声（噪声强度两档），网格灭火域同时带智能体开放与任务开放。基线是六个主流中心化训练方法，统一训练步数预算、统一调参、固定随机种子，评估用一百个留出环境种子并做带校正的配对秩和检验。
结果是九个设置里八个拿到最好，且从不显著差于任何基线；在其中五个设置上显著优于全部六个基线。信息鸿沟最宽的目标发现域上优势最明显，这符合直觉——鸿沟越大，渐进撤回越有价值。消融也支持机制解释：把门强行关掉，损失最大的是开放场景下的灭火域，正是局部视角最容易误导的地方；而在两个无鸿沟的控制组上，门恒为关闭，所有变体返回完全相同的数值。
值得称赞的是作者没有只报对自己有利的数字。在开放性更强的一档灭火设置上，最佳基线的数值反而更高，只是差异不显著；消融里也有变体在个别设置上数值超过完整方法。作者的解释很坦率：门追踪的是符号分歧这个信号，而不是在变体里最大化回报。这种把不利结果连同解释一起写出来的做法，比单纯堆高表格更可信。
怎么读这篇

这是 2026 年 10 月 27 日的预印本，来自内布拉斯加大学林肯分校的团队。实验规范在同类预印本里属于扎实的那一档：固定步数预算、用调参框架给所有基线公平调参、留出一百个评估种子、配对检验带多重比较校正。局限也要看清：每个域只隔离一种鸿沟形式，真实场景往往是叠加的；未处理智能体自身能力或目标发生变化的更一般的开放形式；门只纠正符号分歧，当两种读取彼此一致却同时出错时它无能为力；另外它没有在标准合作基准上测，所以不能直接和那些榜单上的数字比。
对做多智能体系统的工程团队，这套「一个评论家读两遍」几乎是即插即用的：成本近零、不需要新增参数、也不需要改执行架构。更广义的一条是评估习惯——训练时的曲线好看说明不了部署效果，报告执行性能、并且专门设置几个信息鸿沟最大的场景来压测，才看得出方法到底解决了什么问题。

理论主线集中在「与无遗憾学习者的博弈」上：同日出现两篇同组作者的复杂度刻画（优化者能榨取多少战略剩余、以及这种策略优化何时是难解的），再加上这篇联合无遗憾的不可能性，三条拼起来是一个完整故事——多智能体在线学习的收敛性正在被系统地证伪，而不是被补上更好的界。
拍卖与机制设计出现两条并行的线：一条是把先验信息压到只剩区间，最优机制随之分裂成「随机保留价」「池化」「两者随机化」三段结构；另一条是把经典算法博弈论的工具搬进链上，用「预算托管可执行」替换「身份不可伪造」，换来抗女巫与抗重排序。两条的共同点是：当假设被削弱时，最优解会长成反直觉的形状。
过程监督从推理模型外溢到搜索智能体。最有迁移价值的两条结论都很具体：一是基于采样的过程奖励在检索场景会失灵，因为答案可以靠记忆猜对；二是「好的搜索」可以训在小模型上再迁移给大模型用，准确率有实打实的提升。

radar.title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
radar.summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

radar.title: Robust Auction Design with Support Information
radar.summary: A seller wants to sell an item to n buyers. Buyer valuations are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) according to a distribution unknown to the seller; the seller only knows that the support is included in [a, b]. To be robust, the seller chooses a dominant strategy incentive compatible mechanism that optimizes the worst-case performance relative to the ideal expected revenue the seller could have collected with knowledge of buyers’ valuations. Our analysis unifies the regret and the ratio objectives. For these objectives, we derive an optimal mechanism and the corresponding performance in quasi-closed form, as a function of the support information [a, b] and the number of buyers n. Our analysis reveals three regimes of support information and a new class of robust mechanisms. (i) When a/b is below a threshold, the optimal mechanism is a second-price auction (SPA) with random reserve, a focal class in earlier literature. (ii) When a/b is above another threshold, SPAs are strictly suboptimal, and an optimal mechanism belongs to a class of mechanisms we introduce, which we call pooling auctions (POOL); whenever the highest value is above a threshold, the mechanism still allocates to the highest bidder, but otherwise the mechanism allocates to a uniformly random buyer, that is, pools low types. (iii) When a/b is between two thresholds, a randomization between SPA and POOL is optimal. We also characterize optimal mechanisms within nested central subclasses of mechanisms: standard mechanisms that only allocate to the highest bidder, SPA with random reserve, and SPA with no reserve. We show strict separations in terms of performance across classes, implying that deviating from standard mechanisms is necessary for robustness. Lastly, we show that the same results hold under other distribution classes that capture “positive dependence,” namely i.i.d., mixture of i.i.d., and exchangeable and affiliated distributions, as well as i.i.d. regular distributions. radar.title: The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
radar.summary: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

radar.title: Public Signals in Affine Network Congestion Games with Uncertain Free-Flow Times
radar.summary: Travel times in road networks are subject to stochastic uncertainty resulting from various parameters. A benevolent mobility service provider observing the actual travel times from data may use its informational advantage to steer the traffic equilibrium in a favorable direction through a processs known as signaling or Bayesian persuasion. Previous work has shown that the underlying signaling problem can be NP-hard to approximate better than [Formula: see text], even for static Wardrop flows with affine cost functions with stochastic offsets. In contrast, we show that in this case, the signaling problem is easy for many networks. First, we tightly characterize the class of single-commodity networks in which full information revelation is always an optimal signaling strategy. Second, we construct a reduction from optimal signaling to computing an optimal collection of active edges for the Wardrop equilibrium. For two states, this allows us to efficiently compute an optimal signaling scheme whenever the number of different active edge sets is bounded by a polynomial in the input size. Using a cell decomposition technique, we extend the approach to a polynomial-time algorithm for multicommodity parallel-edge networks provided that both the number of commodities and states are constant. radar.title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
radar.summary: Abstract Knowledge-constrained network inference enables the reconstruction of regulatory programmes from high-dimensional biological data, yet the conditions under which shared and context-specific structures can be reliably identified remain poorly understood. Pablo Rodriguez-Mier et al. recently introduced CORNETO, a framework for multi-sample constrained inference. Here we reproduce, evaluate and extend CORNETO in terms of robustness, identifiability and bias–variance trade-offs. Using dynamic haematopoiesis and stable cortical datasets, we systematically assess four network reconstruction paradigms while preserving the original method-specific evaluation procedures and benchmark definitions. We show that multi-sample inference generally improves robustness and reproducibility, although gains in predictive performance depend on biological context and the completeness of the prior network. To enhance stability, we introduce bootstrap aggregation and selective re-expansion strategies that improve consensus robustness and recovery while preserving context-specific signals without modifying the underlying optimization scheme or sacrificing generality. Across datasets and methods, our results reveal distinct inference regimes governed by sample availability, prior knowledge and regularization. Together, these findings position network reconstruction as a regime-dependent learning problem and provide practical principles for robust multi-sample biological network inference.

radar.title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
radar.summary: Abstract The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

radar.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

radar.summary: Multi-agent navigation is a fundamental problem in robotics, autonomous vehicles, warehouse automation, traffic management, and other systems in which several autonomous entities must reach individual destinations while sharing limited space. Classical Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) focuses on producing collision-free paths, whereas Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) learns policies through interaction and can adapt to changing agent behavior. This literature paper reviews the foundations of reinforcement learning, Q-learning, Deep Q-Networks (DQN), multi-agent reinforcement learning, coordination, collision avoidance, centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE), and learning-based multiagent pathfinding. The literature identifies non-stationarity, partial observability, joint action complexity, reward design, communication overhead, scalability, and evaluation consistency as recurring challenges. Based on these findings, GridMind is positioned as a controlled research environment in which multiple agents learn navigation policies in a discrete grid while the same environment is rendered as an interactive 3D simula-tion. A staged approach—random baseline, Q-learning, DQN, independent multi-agent learning, and coordinated learning—provides an understandable and experimentally defensible pathway for studying learned coordination.

radar.title: Multiagent Assortment Optimization in Sequential Matching Markets
radar.summary: Motivated by the challenges faced by choice-based matching platforms, in this work, we study a generalization of the two-sided assortment optimization model. Specifically, this model consists of two sides (e.g., customers and suppliers) who have preferences over the opposite side in the form of discrete choice models. A matching is realized through a two-step process where the platform’s decision is to initially present to each agent on one side an assortment of users of the opposite side. The ultimate goal of the platform is to maximize the total expected revenue collected from the matching. Because of the computational complexity of this problem, we focus on the design of approximation algorithms with constant-factor guarantees for the constrained version of the problem under general choice preferences. First, to the best of our knowledge, we are the first to draw connections with the literature of submodular optimization and show that one-sided choice-oblivious approaches perform arbitrarily badly. Second, we show that, for the general setting, there exists a two-sided choice-aware randomized algorithm that achieves a [Formula: see text]-approximation factor, which is the best possible. Third, we design an algorithm that is asymptotically optimal when one side follows the well-known multinomial logit (MNL) choice model under the small probability regime. Fourth, we provide a simple and effective algorithm with a [Formula: see text]-approximation guarantee for the unconstrained setting, with both sides following MNL models. Finally, we assess the performance of our proposed methods with a detailed computational study and discuss several extensions. Funding: M. radar.title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
radar.venue_raw: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
radar.summary: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic “gatekeeper,” regulating oxidation through a “breathing mode” of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a “rupture mode” leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

An Analysis of Zero-Sum Game Agent Training Based on Large Language Models and Self-Play Mechanisms
radar.summary: This paper carries out a review of competitive agent training under zero‑sum game settings, analysing persistent drawbacks found in traditional self‑play reinforcement learning, including inflexible decision‑making policies and weak long‑horizon reasoning capacity. Game agents built purely upon large language models are incapable of sustaining iterative upgrades amid ongoing adversarial contests. Accordingly, the present work investigates viable integration schemes that unite large language models and self‑play training systems. It first lays out the definition of zero‑sum games, illustrates standard self‑play training workflows, and revisits fundamental algorithms from game theory. Four practical integration patterns are classified, namely auxiliary policy generation, reward evaluation optimisation, accumulation of adversarial experience, and the construction of diversified training opponents. Relying on theoretical formula derivation and comparative experimental statistics, this paper evaluates widely adopted modern frameworks against five core benchmarks: reasoning performance, training productivity, generalisation capability, computational expenditure, and training stability, so as to compare their distinct strengths and weaknesses. Evaluation findings indicate that each standalone integration paradigm bears intrinsic flaws. Frameworks adopting dynamically‑generated opponents deliver optimal generalisation performance, while optimised reward mechanisms enable the fastest training convergence. Nonetheless, all hybrid training architectures confront common bottlenecks such as LLM hallucination, prohibitive computational overhead, and oscillating gradient signals during model training. This review identifies several high‑potential research directions: dynamic multi‑module collaborative structures, streamlined self‑play workflows, retrieval‑augmented technologies to restrain hallucination, as well as the development of general‑purpose game agents. The outcomes of this analysis can supply theoretical references for future advances in adversarial decision‑making artificial intelligence.

radar.title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
radar.summary: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

Sybil-Proofness of Generalized Adaptive Clinching and Implications for Blockchain Mechanism Design
radar.summary: The adaptive clinching auction of Dobzinski, Lavi, and Nisan (FOCS'08) is a cornerstone of mechanism design with budget-constrained bidders, and it has since inspired a broad range of extensions to substantially richer market settings. Adaptive clinching enjoys compelling guarantees: it is Pareto optimal, and truthful bidding is a dominant strategy whenever budgets cannot be overreported. In many real-world environments, however, identities are cheap to create, making resilience to Sybil attacks an additional requirement. Whether the guarantees of adaptive clinching survive when a bidder can split its budget across fake identities has remained open. We introduce a generalized framework for adaptive clinching and prove that it satisfies Sybil-robust incentive compatibility: a bidder cannot benefit from splitting into any finite number of identities with arbitrary value reports, provided their aggregate reported budget does not exceed the bidder's enforceable true budget. Sybil resilience thus joins the list of ideal properties of adaptive clinching. Our work is motivated by practical problems in decentralized finance, where automated market makers (AMMs) are among the most widely used applications. We design a new AMM mechanism that extends classical adaptive clinching in two ways: it supports a two-sided market and protects against two-sided strategies, and it allows the supply function to depend on the auction state. Its one-sided special case is captured by our generalized adaptive clinching framework, and our proof techniques show that the full two-sided mechanism simultaneously satisfies Sybil-robust incentive compatibility and a relaxed notion of Pareto optimality. We argue that these guarantees are essentially the best possible via impossibility results. More broadly, our work reveals new connections between classical algorithmic game theory and modern decentralized blockchains.

radar.title: On the Maximization of Long-Run Conditional Value-at-Risk for Markov Decision Processes
radar.summary: Optimizing Risk-Seeking Sequential Decisions via Conditional Value-at-Risk Decision makers may exhibit risk-seeking preferences in finance, energy operations, and stochastic resource management, yet corresponding Markov decision process (MDP) theories remain underdeveloped. In this paper, “On the Maximization of Long-Run CVaR for Markov Decision Processes,” Xia, Yu, and Wu investigate infinite-horizon MDPs maximizing long-run conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) for instantaneous rewards. They prove optimality for stationary randomized policies and show deterministic policies may fail; an optimal policy randomizes over at most two actions. By converting the original problem into a minimax saddle point formulation, the authors develop solvable linear programming and globally convergent gradient descent algorithms. Results are further extended to joint mean-CVaR optimization and validated on real-world microgrid scheduling data. This work fills gaps for risk-seeking MDPs and delivers practical computation tools for tail-oriented sequential decision making.

radar.title: Impossibility of No-Regret in Multi-Agent Bidding
radar.summary: We consider $T$ repeated second-price auctions across $n$ pacing bidders with i.i.d. item arrivals, and show that it is computationally impossible for all bidders to achieve no-regret simultaneously while satisfying their respective budget or return-on-investment constraints. Therefore, in the prominent internet auction systems where buyers simultaneously deploy pacing algorithms or automated bidding agents, we cannot hope to achieve joint no-regret guarantees in general. We establish a deterministic relationship that high variance in online bidding systems implies high regret. By showing that one can extract a pacing equilibrium from a low-variance system, we prove PPAD-hardness of attaining joint no-regret. For several widely used bidding algorithms, we also show evidence from dynamical systems and numerical simulations that they can indeed display high-variance behavior through cycling, even on simple market instances.

radar.title: Bargaining and Contract Forms in Distribution Channels: Why Do Slotting Fees Arise and Linear Contracts Persist?
radar.summary: Two empirical patterns emerge in business-to-business settings, particularly in retail distribution channels such as grocery markets. First, linear contracts are widely observed alongside nonlinear contracts with fixed payments, despite the claimed efficiency advantages of the latter. Second, when fixed payments arise, they often flow from suppliers to retailers (slotting fees) rather than the reverse. We develop and analyze a model of multilateral bargaining in which a supplier negotiates separately with competing retailers to explain these patterns. The key mechanism is a trade-off between two distortions: under linear contracts, wholesale prices reflect bargaining power and can be either above or below the channel-profit-maximizing level, whereas under two-part tariffs, wholesale prices are set to maximize bilateral surplus independently of bargaining power but are systematically too low from an overall channel perspective because of rent shifting across relationships. As a result, neither contractual form uniformly dominates; instead, relative performance depends on how bargaining shapes gains from trade across firms. When bargaining leads to slotting fees, two-part tariffs yield higher channel profits than linear contracts, whereas when it would imply payments from retailers to suppliers, linear contracts may perform better. These findings offer a unified explanation for the persistence of linear contracts alongside two-part tariffs, the direction of fixed payments, and the conditions under which each contractual form is likely to arise. This paper was accepted by Miguel Villas-Boas, marketing. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.03426 .

radar.title: Cyber Defence, Agentic AI, and the Sociotechnical Paradigm: A Survey of AI-Driven Cybersecurity
radar.venue: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies
radar.venue_raw: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies
radar.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping cybersecurity, moving it from signature-based reactive security to agentic, self-evolving, and proactive operations. However, the fast deployment of autonomous agents entails significant security issues, physical-layer attacks in cyber-physical systems, alignment problems, and advanced social engineering risks jeopardizing the stability of the modern sociotechnical infrastructures. This survey paper, which summarizes and analyses the literature, examines the duality of AI in cybersecurity, exploring its implications for strengthening digital defences and increasing the threat landscape for adversaries. We perform a thorough review of 36 cutting-edge research articles, which are organized into six important areas: self-evolving defensive paradigms, LLM-based intelligent agents, reinforcement learning for autonomous decision-making, security of cyber-physical systems, human-machine co-teaming, and agent alignment. Our synthesis shows that multi-agent collaborations greatly shorten incident response times and automate discovery of vulnerabilities but are also highly vulnerable to prompt injection, training data poisoning, and physical-layer spoofing. Moreover, we identify a shift from model patches to model alignment and constitutional safety at runtime as a prerequisite for securing these systems. We believe that resilient digital defence must also be considered a sociotechnical problem, as there must be agents, autonomous systems, that are governed by other agents, aligned and constitutionally bound, and are able to collaborate, rather than operate completely separately, with human operators.

radar.title: Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange
radar.summary: Unlocking Value Through Nonprofit Resource Sharing Nonprofit organizations often operate under tight budgets while idle equipment, unused space, and shareable skills and expertise are frequently underutilized, with existing resource exchanges in the nonprofit sector limited to bilateral barter or relatively homogeneous resources. In “Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange,” Huang et al. propose Sharing With a Purpose (SWAP), a resource-sharing system that enables nonprofits to exchange heterogeneous resources without monetary payments. The authors implement this market design through the SWAP Hub, a digital platform deployed with nonprofit communities in multiple regions. Through repeated exchange episodes, participating organizations have shared not only physical assets but also a wide range of skills, services, and expertise, including marketing, management, event planning, and organizational development. radar.title: Noise Shapes the Surplus: Strategic Play Against No-Regret Learners
radar.summary: Recent work has shown that, in zero-sum games, an optimizer can extract $Ω(\sqrt{T})$ strategic surplus---cumulative payoff above the minimax benchmark---against noiseless no-regret learners with a constant step size. However, in practice, learners often act on perturbed payoff scores and use decaying learning rates $η_t$. Since existing extraction mechanisms rely on exact scores, a natural question is whether noise shields the learner from exploitation and eliminates surplus altogether. We address this question for the widely used class of Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) algorithms. Under standard regularity conditions, we establish three results, none of which assumes independence of the noise. First, under summability conditions, passive play of a strategy fixed independently of the horizon earns at most constant surplus. Second, we design a new mechanism that exploits the learner's noise-dependent response: a clairvoyant optimizer who knows the update rule and the limiting mean response secures $Ω(1/η_T)$ surplus whenever that mean is profitable. Third, even when that mean is not profitable, active alternating play extracts $Ω(\sum_{t<T}η_t)$ surplus by exploiting the learner's movement rather than its location, under suitable responsiveness and stability conditions. Finally, at the canonical learning rate $η_t\propto t^{-1/2}$, we recover the noiseless $Ω(\sqrt{T})$ rate for mean-zero, finite-variance perturbations---whether fresh with arbitrary temporal dependence or accumulated from i.i.d. increments---provided the limiting mean response is profitable.

radar.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
radar.summary: Objective: This study aims to determine whether a hip-exoskeleton policy trained in simulation, by co-adapting with a musculoskeletal human model under a metabolic-energy reward, reduces the metabolic cost of walking in new users without per-user tuning, and how mechanical-power shaping affects the learned assistance. Methods: We developed MARL-Exo, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which a full-body human model (304 muscle actuators; randomized anatomy, gait, and speed) and a bilateral hip-exoskeleton policy are trained concurrently in two stages. The exoskeleton observes only delayed hip kinematics and its past commands; its reward includes muscle metabolic power from a physiologically based energetics model, alone (Metabolic) or with mechanical-power shaping (Metabolic + Power). The Metabolic policy was deployed and tested without retraining in eight healthy adults walking at 1.25 m/s, using indirect calorimetry. Results: In simulation, the Metabolic policy reduced modeled muscle metabolic power by 13.8% relative to no-device walking, versus 8.8% for Metabolic + Power. On hardware, MARL-Exo reduced net metabolic rate by 18.3 $\pm$ 6.6% relative to Passive in all eight participants. Relative to No-Exo, the mean reduction was 7.4 $\pm$ 10.0%; six participants more than offset the 13.1% device-wearing penalty, walking up to 24.2% below their No-Exo cost. Conclusion: A metabolically informed policy co-adapted in simulation transferred to users without per-user tuning and consistently reduced the metabolic cost of walking with the device, while explicit power shaping reduced the simulated benefit. Significance: Unlike per-user human-in-the-loop optimization, this approach yields a single population-level controller and allows assistance objectives to be screened in simulation before human testing.

radar.title: A Survey of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from the Perspective of Task Characteristics
radar.summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), the relationship between agents' rewards determines part of the learning problem. Shared rewards give rise to credit assignment and coordinated action selection; opposed rewards require responses to an adapting opponent. Both relationships occur in mixed tasks. This survey takes these task differences as the starting point for reviewing MARL, complementing classifications based on algorithms, training frameworks, or application domains. The analysis follows task characteristics, interaction types, and algorithmic mechanisms across cooperative, competitive, and mixed cooperative-competitive settings. It covers the basic formulations and training and execution paradigms, then compares representative methods in terms of their mechanisms, applicability, and limitations. Path planning, task allocation, pursuit-evasion and adversarial engagement, autonomous driving, and resource allocation illustrate how information access and operational constraints affect method selection. The concluding discussion concerns non-stationarity, scaling, safety, and the evidence needed for deployment. The comparisons support method selection under stated task conditions, without treating applicability as independent of the task being addressed.

radar.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Environment for Beyond-Visual-Range Air Combat
radar.summary: An open simulation environment is presented for training multiple reinforcement-learning agents in beyond-visual-range air combat while balancing physical fidelity against rollout speed. The objective is to provide a reproducible testbed that retains the sensing, tracking, weapon, and cooperative-information effects governing long-range engagements without the computational cost of a full mission simulator. Aircraft and missiles use geodetic four-degree-of-freedom kinematics and energy-based aerodynamics; probabilistic radar detections, electronic-warfare effects, shared-track fusion, seeker-constrained missile guidance, and distance-dependent terminal lethality are represented explicitly. Fixed-shape observations and safety-gated actions support parallel self-play. End-to-end experiments with a memoryless policy learned boundary compliance, survival, and progressively more effective weapon employment, while subsystem profiling measured approximately ten seconds of wall-clock time for a 300-step two-versus-two episode on the reported hardware. These results establish internal training readiness and reproducible computational scaling and form a platform for reproducible research on learned tactics and fair benchmarking in this domain.
radar.summary_short: An open simulation environment is presented for training multiple reinforcement-learning agents in beyond-visual-range air combat while balancing physical fidelity against rollout speed.

radar.title: Single and multi-winner auctions with performance obligation
radar.summary: Auctioning access rights to private providers through competitive tendering has become a central instrument for governments to regulate markets and public services. While efficient in allocating licenses, such auctions may generate monopolistic market structures with adverse effects on consumer welfare. We experimentally evaluate two policy interventions to mitigate these outcomes: introducing post-tender competition and imposing minimum production obligations on winning firms. Our results show that performance obligations substantially improve welfare by raising output and consumer surplus, albeit at the cost of reduced auction revenue. Extending the design with additional treatments, we demonstrate that genuine competition yields even stronger welfare gains. These findings highlight a trade-off between government revenue and consumer welfare in auction design. We conclude that while obligations are an effective tool to counter monopoly distortions, sustaining competition remains essential to maximise total surplus at the market level.

radar.title: AI Digital Twin for Cloud Cyber Security
radar.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
radar.venue_raw: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
radar.summary: The key advantage of cloud computing is scalability and flexibility of infrastructure, however, the growing complexity of cloud environments has led to numerous security issues. Current security systems are largely reactive, which means that any detected attacks have already taken place. This paper suggests the use of the AI-based Digital Twin technology for cybersecurity in cloud environments, providing the possibility of creating a virtual copy of the cloud environment that can be used for continuous monitoring, attack simulation, and security testing. The proposed framework uses AI/ML algorithms for anomaly detection, attacks' classification, and risk assessment in conjunction with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) in order to achieve collaboration and adaptability of security response. The system includes cloud resource monitoring, attacks simulation, security logging, alert generation, access control by roles, and security analysis dashboard. The development of the system takes place using MERN stack architecture with Digital Twin synchronization of virtual cloud resources and their metrics. With the combination of Digital Twin technology, AI-based threat detection and multi-agent decision making, the proposed framework can provide enhanced proactivity,adaptiveness, and real-time performance of cybersecurity in cloud environments.

radar.title: Autonomous biomedical research with an artificial intelligence agent
radar.summary: Biomedical research is increasingly constrained by repetitive, fragmented workflows that slow discovery. We introduce Biomni, a general-purpose biomedical artificial intelligence agent that autonomously executes diverse research tasks. To map the biomedical action space, Biomni’s action-discovery agent mines tools, databases, and protocols from thousands of publications across 25 domains, building a unified agentic environment. Its general-purpose architecture integrates large language model reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, dynamically composing workflows without predefined templates. Systematic benchmarking shows strong generalization across heterogeneous tasks—causal gene prioritization, drug repurposing, rare-disease diagnosis, microbiome analysis, and molecular cloning—without task-specific tuning. Real-world case studies demonstrate Biomni interpreting multimodal datasets, optimizing protein stability, orchestrating wet-lab instruments, and generating experimentally testable protocols. Biomni envisions artificial intelligence augmenting human scientists and accelerating discovery.

radar.title: TANDEM: Balancing Centralized and Decentralized Critics to Address the Information Gap in Complex Multi-Agent Environments
radar.summary: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) shapes decentralized policies with a centralized critic that observes the global state, then removes the critic at execution. The policies are optimized to rely on information they will not have when they act, an information gap between training and execution. It widens under partial observability, observation noise, and openness, where the set of agents and tasks present changes during an episode. Existing methods transfer centralized guidance in one direction only, removing or distilling the critic once, so the policies never rehearse acting without the critic while they can still be corrected. We propose TANDEM, which keeps one centralized critic and reads it two ways at each training step: a centralized read from the global state, and a decentralized read restricted to the information each agent will have at execution. A parameter-free gate compares the two reads for each agent and trains the policy on the decentralized read where they agree, reinstating the centralized read only where the local view is misleading. A shared target pulls the decentralized read toward the centralized one. We formalize the setting as a task- and agent-open decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (TAO-Dec-POMDP) and evaluate TANDEM on three cooperative domains, each isolating one form of the information gap: discovery for partial observability, sampling for observation noise, and openness in wildfire suppression. We compare against six CTDE baselines and ablate the gate and the shared target; the supplementary material holds the full variant sweep, diagnostics, and learning curves. We measure return at execution, once the centralized critic is removed. TANDEM is the best method on eight of the nine setups and never significantly worse than any baseline.
radar.summary_short: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) shapes decentralized policies with a centralized critic that observes the global state, then removes the critic at execution.

radar.title: Toward unified intelligence in renewable-dominant power systems: a survey of hybrid forecasting, explainable AI, and multi-agent optimization
radar.summary: The transition toward renewable-dominant power systems has introduced significant operational challenges due to increased uncertainty, reduced system inertia, and the proliferation of distributed energy resources. While artificial intelligence (AI) techniques have been widely adopted for renewable energy forecasting and grid optimization, existing studies primarily address these components in isolation, leading to fragmented system-level intelligence. This paper presents a comprehensive survey that systematically integrates three critical dimensions of modern intelligent energy systems: hybrid forecasting, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and multi-agent optimization. First, we review advanced hybrid learning architectures, including decomposition-based models, ensemble frameworks, and deep learning-metaheuristic hybrids, highlighting their effectiveness in capturing nonlinear and stochastic renewable dynamics. Second, we examine XAI techniques that enhance transparency, interpretability, and trust in AI-driven energy systems. Third, we analyze the evolution from centralized optimization to distributed collective intelligence using multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), swarm intelligence, and federated learning paradigms. Unlike conventional surveys, this work provides a unified system-level perspective by explicitly linking predictive uncertainty with decentralized decision-making and explainability mechanisms. A conceptual integration framework is presented to demonstrate how probabilistic forecasting, risk-aware MARL policies, and interpretable models can jointly enable robust and scalable grid operation. Furthermore, we identify key research challenges related to scalability, computational efficiency, uncertainty propagation, and real-time deployment. This survey offers a structured reference for researchers and practitioners and outlines future directions toward trustworthy, adaptive, and cooperative AI-driven energy systems.
radar.summary_short: The transition toward renewable-dominant power systems has introduced significant operational challenges due to increased uncertainty, reduced system inertia, and the proliferation of distributed energy resources.

radar.title: Implementation via political parties
radar.summary: We address the implementation of public policies (alternatives) when the feasible set is unknown to the planner. The implementing agents are the political parties, who know the feasible set. They care about the implemented alternative, which reflects their ideology, and their share in parliament and office. They face a mechanism that, given the alternatives proposed by all parties, asks the voters to rank them and determines the chosen alternative and the shares in parliament and office. We identify conditions on parties’ preferences that guarantee the socially optimal policy is the outcome of the unique pure strategy Nash equilibrium of the electoral game played by the parties. The existence of the equilibrium does not require any assumptions about the parties’ ideology. To ensure uniqueness, shares must prevail over ideology: office or parliamentary shares in two-party systems, and strictly office shares in systems with more than two parties.

radar.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Evaluating and Mitigating Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
radar.summary: In the world of large language models (LLMs), prompt injection attacks are a severe security risk that can circumvent the instructions given to AI agents and potentially cause damage. In agentic architectures, the vulnerabilities are magnified because of the increased attack surfaces which are present in the use of tools, APIs and chains of reasoning. The vulnerabilities are compounded in agentic architectures as the tools used, APIs called, and chains of reasoning become a larger attack surface, resulting in an increased sense of unreliability. Paraphrased, adaptive, and context-aware attacks are not thwarted by rule-based and static prompt engineering defenses. This paper introduces a deep learning-based approach to detecting and thwarting prompt injection attacks in LLM agent systems. Uses a hybrid model of known and customer-generated adversarial prompts to combine transformer-based classification, semantic risk-scoring and adaptive mitigation procedures. Stratified data splits are used in the experiments, as are synthetic attack generation and rule-based, BERT and zero-shot LLM classifiers. In terms of precision, recall, F1 score and AUC, the proposed framework is found to be better than all the baselines. Attack of instruction override, data extraction and tool misuse are greatly enhanced and resistant to adversarial scenarios that are not seen and adaptable. The mitigation module achieves high task utility; low false positive rates and the high success rate of the attacks is significantly reduced. Overall, the framework demonstrates that it is possible to integrate detection, risk estimation, and mitigation in a single pipeline, resulting in a great improvement in the security of LLM agents, while not burdening them with significant computing costs. It further highlights the importance of security layers before deploying LLM agents to the real world as the input they receive can be adversarial and continuously change, requiring a mixture of machine learning and structured control to ensure they remain safe and reliable across different application areas. Scalable AI systems deployment safety improvements involve multi-agent security, real-time learning, and multimodal prompt injection detection in the future.

radar.title: The Complexity of Strategizing Against No-Regret Learners: Pure When It Is Easy, Hard Even When Mixed
radar.summary: We study the computational complexity of clairvoyant strategy optimization against a known online learner in finite-horizon repeated games. In general-sum games with bounded payoffs, unless $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$, no polynomial-time optimizer can achieve a reward within $cT$ of the reward of the optimal pure-action sequence for an absolute constant $c>0$, even when allowed to output explicitly represented mixed strategies at every round. Our hardness result strengthens prior work along two complementary axes: it extends to a broader class of learning dynamics, including widely used mean-based algorithms, answering an open question of Assos, Dagan, and Rajaraman (2025) for learners beyond multiplicative weights; and it permits mixed outputs while retaining the weaker pure-sequence benchmark. Thus, neither mixed strategies nor algorithmic specificity removes the computational obstruction in general-sum games. In sharp contrast, zero-sum games exhibit the reverse phenomenon: deterministic pure actions suffice for efficiently recovering the leading surplus guarantees previously obtained through mixed play against Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) opponents. Thus, the two regimes form a striking mirror image: mixed play cannot overcome general-sum hardness even against a pure benchmark, whereas pure play retains the full surplus guarantees of mixed strategies in zero-sum games.

radar.title: Online LLM Inference Routing for Multi-Agent Systems under Long-Term Budget and Layered Privacy Constraints
radar.summary: Abstract The Cloud-Edge-End (CEE) collaborative architecture has become a key paradigm for deploying highly intelligent multi-agent systems with low latency and high energy efficiency. Existing studies on efficient task offloading in CEE, however, either overlook long-term financial budget constraints from commercial API token usage and edge computing leasing, or inadequately handle layered information-sharing and privacy restrictions in decentralized autonomous agents. This paper investigates online inference routing to minimize the computational and communication overhead of large language model (LLM) workloads under long-term budget constraints, agent intent-sharing limitations, and un-known future prompt lengths. We propose a budget-aware online optimization framework that uses Lyapunov optimization to decouple long-term financial constraints, and show that the decoupled problem forms a generalized ordinal potential game. To address heterogeneous information-sharing restrictions, we design an adaptive best response algorithm for cooperative environments with shared decision information, and a multi-agent distributed routing algorithm for limited-information environments, enabling efficient offloading without inter-agent intent sharing. Theoretical analysis provides conditional performance and queue-length bounds and establishes finite convergence of the per-slot solvers. Simulations on distributed inference testbeds show that our scheme reduces the inference overhead of heterogeneous agentic tasks while achieving a favorable trade-off between performance and actual token expenditure.
radar.summary_short: Abstract The Cloud-Edge-End (CEE) collaborative architecture has become a key paradigm for deploying highly intelligent multi-agent systems with low latency and high energy efficiency.

radar.title: Preference-Guided Cooperation in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.summary: Multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning (MOMARL) addresses agent coordination and objective trade-offs simultaneously while optimising overall system performance. Existing work tends to treat multi-agent cooperation and multi-objective optimisation as largely independent components of a learning problem, which amounts to an exorbitant complexity except in trivial cases. We study here whether the structure provided by multiple objectives can itself be exploited to facilitate cooperation, rather than being treated as an additional optimisation challenge. We formulate MOMARL at both the team and individual levels and introduce objective-wise counterfactual credit assignment to evaluate each agent's contribution across the team objectives. We propose Meta-Gradient Informed Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MIRL), with static (MIRL-S) and dynamic (MIRL-D) variants. By incorporating meta-gradient information, MIRL enables agents to learn how to prioritise objectives individually while collectively optimising the system-level objective, allowing the multi-objective structure to directly guide cooperation. Experiments on a multi-objective multiple particle environment show that our methods improve Pareto-front quality over baselines, with the dynamic variant achieving the strongest performance.

radar.title: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
radar.summary: Recent work has explored optimizing LLM collaboration through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), but many approaches still rely on predefined workflows, limiting efficiency and scalability. Decentralized LLM collaboration is challenging because agents execute independently with limited communication, share a joint objective, and must infer useful information from communication traces. In this paper, we propose BCMAAC, a Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor-Critic method that maintains beliefs over contextual information and uses them to facilitate training. Experiments on Minecraft game-playing, web searching and tool-using tasks show that BCMAAC improves task performance and collaborative behavior compared to naive actor-critic baselines. The improvements are particularly pronounced in multi-turn tasks with richer contextual information, where belief modeling provides a clear advantage.

radar.title: Context-Aware Cooperative Gating for Knowledge-Controlled Value Factorization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.venue: International Journal of Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering
radar.venue_raw: International Journal of Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering
radar.summary: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under partial observability requires decentralized agents to act from incomplete local information. Value-decomposition methods such as VDN and QMIX do not control when teammate-related knowledge may influence an agent’s local utility, and an uncontrolled teammate-conditioned term can distort decisions at timesteps where no ally is observable. We propose CA-QMIX, a context-aware value factorization method that uses ally visibility as a knowledge signal for decentralized agent control. Each agent combines an individual decision branch with an attention-based cooperative knowledge branch through a visibility-conditioned gate that scales the cooperative contribution and is hard-masked to zero when no ally is observable. The gated utilities are combined by a QMIX-style monotonic mixer, which we prove preserves Individual-Global-Max consistency, and a mixer-level Δ-Q regularizer discourages cooperative corrections that lower the greedy value of the base branch. Experiments on seven SMAC v1 and SMAC v2 scenarios against six value-decomposition baselines show that CA-QMIX attains the highest mean final win rate and the best mean rank over the seven scenarios and improves on QMIX in all three randomized SMAC v2 scenarios. Ablations show that most of the gain comes from the cooperative branch, that its visibility conditioning helps when correctly aligned (misaligned visibility degrades performance under randomized placement), and that the form of the gate is not critical: a binary gate suffices and the hard no-ally mask has no measurable cost.

radar.title: Collective Emergent Alignment: Measuring and Amplifying Interaction-Induced Reasoning Alignment in Multi-Agent LLMs
radar.summary: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems can exhibit emergent behaviors through interaction, yet whether a similar phenomenon exists for reasoning alignment remains largely unexplored. We study whether agent interaction produces additional reference-grounded reasoning alignment beyond matched individual self-refinement, and introduce REMAP (Reference-Entailment-Matrix for Agentic Process), a framework that quantifies this effect through Semantic Coverage and interaction-specific alignment gains. Across diverse model families and two multi-hop reasoning benchmarks, we observe broadly positive interaction gains, particularly on reasoning content that depends on integrating evidence distributed across agents. These gains are consistently associated with independently measured peer-information recovery, while further analysis reveals composition-dependent heterogeneity effects and asymmetric information transfer across agent capability levels. Motivated by these findings, we further introduce a fact-level multi-agent communication framework that replaces full reasoning-trace exchange with compact, gap-aware, and selectively routed information. Our experiments show that compact fact exchange improves reasoning alignment and task performance while reducing communication overhead, whereas more selective communication exposes a trade-off between acquiring distributed information, retaining local content, and communication efficiency. Overall, our results show that collective emergent alignment can be quantified, linked to information-transfer patterns, and used to guide more effective multi-agent communication.

radar.title: Centralized Critics for N-Agent Ad Hoc Teamwork
radar.summary: Centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) has become the dominant paradigm in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), motivating extensive study of what privileged information should be made available to the critic during training. While prior work has examined the role of global state in fully cooperative settings, the design of centralized critics for N-agent ad hoc teamwork - in which dynamically varying set of learning agents must coordinate with an arbitrary set of uncontrolled teammates drawn from an unknown distribution - remains poorly understood. We study this question by comparing two natural classes of advantage estimators: controlled history estimators, which condition only on the observation and action histories of the learner's own agents, and joint history estimators, which additionally condition on the histories of the uncontrolled teammates. We prove that both estimators are unbiased and characterize the conditions under which the joint history estimate attains strictly lower variance than its controlled counterpart. Empirically, joint history critics match or outperform controlled history critics across a range of NAHT tasks, yielding improved sample efficiency and final returns. Together, these results provide both a theoretical justification and an empirical recommendation for incorporating uncontrolled agent histories into centralized critics for N-agent ad hoc teamwork.

In Which Matching Markets Do Costly Compatibility Inspections Lead to a Deadlock?
radar.summary: When Learning About a Match Stalls the Market In many matching markets, participants must investigate whether a match is feasible. When inspection is costly, participants may delay investigating a potential match until both sides have effectively committed. Such caution can cause each side to wait for others to act, creating an “information deadlock.” In their article, “In Which Matching Markets Do Costly Compatibility Inspections Lead to a Deadlock?” Immorlica, Kanoria, and Lu study this problem in random two-sided markets. They characterize how deadlock depends on the market balance, market connectivity, and the chance that inspections succeed. Using statistical physics tools, their analysis identifies phase transitions between deadlock-free and deadlocked markets. The findings offer design guidance: More choice is not always better; match rates are highest at the deadlock phase boundary; and parallel inspections and clearer participant differentiation can reduce the extent to which waiting chains stall the market.

radar.title: Trading Off Business and Family Investments: Evidence from U.S. Entrepreneurial Households
radar.summary: Investing in children’s human capital reduces business investments for U.S. entrepreneurial households. Using financial account data of 90,000 small businesses linked to their owners and a regression discontinuity design that compares the business performance of households with college-aged dependents (18–22) to those with near-college-aged dependents (14–17), I show that business revenues and expenses decline sharply when owners’ children reach age 18. Despite the declines, profitability and productivity remain largely unaffected, suggesting a general downsizing rather than a loss in efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis shows that downsizing is concentrated among highly indebted owner households and businesses with volatile cash flows. For each dollar increase in household spending associated with a child turning 18, business expenses decline by $2.26. These findings are consistent with entrepreneurial parents reallocating capital from business investments toward their children’s human capital, as both compete for the same pool of internal family financial resources. radar.title: Local Algebraic Stability of Wasserstein Gradient Descent-Ascent and Mean Field Langevin Dynamics without Spectral Gap
radar.summary: We study the local stability of Wasserstein gradient descent-ascent (GDA) for entropy regularized two-player zero-sum games on noncompact domains. When one or both equilibrium measures fail to satisfy a Poincaré inequality, the spectral gap arguments underlying local exponential convergence are unavailable. we show that Wasserstein GDA converges algebraically to the mixed Nash equilibrium in chi-squared divergence, provided the initial relative density is a small perturbation in $L^2$ with bounded algebraic moments. The proof has two main ingredients: a cancellation in a negative Sobolev energy estimate, and a bootstrap argument that keeps the moments bounded uniformly in time. For polynomial-tailed equilibria, we construct perturbations supported far out in the tails that survive over diffusive time scales, which gives algebraic lower bounds on the worst-case relaxation rate. We also establish analogous local algebraic stability and lower bound results for mean-field Langevin dynamics, when the equilibrium fails to satisfy a spectral gap.
